TokenScanResult.description:
Normalized verdict for a swap-token security scan.

Branch on this, never on individual `features` — the provider (Blockaid)
already aggregates its features into the verdict, and the feature catalogue
changes underneath us (ids get added, renamed and deprecated).

`UNSCANNED` is the explicit fourth state the ticket calls for: provider
outage, rate limit, timeout, unsupported chain, missing credentials or a
verdict string we don't recognise. It always means *fail open* — an external
scanner being unavailable must never block a swap.

TokenScanFeature.description:
One provider feature. Stored verbatim, with **no allowlist** — Blockaid adds,
renames and deprecates feature ids (INORGANIC_VOLUME is already deprecated),
so hardcoding a subset goes stale. Reference/context for FE copy and admin
visibility only.

type.description: Provider severity for this feature: Malicious | Warning | Benign | Info.

TokenScanUnscannedReason.description: Why a token ended up `UNSCANNED`. Diagnostic only — never a branching input.

provider.description: Screening provider that produced this verdict.

providerResultType.description:

don't model yet is still visible to support instead of being erased.

maliciousScore.description: Provider `malicious_score`, 0..1. Arrives as a string; stored as a number.

expiresAt.description: When this verdict goes stale and the token should be re-scanned.

hasBundler.description:
Indicates whether the token can be used in a bundle (multiswap) swap.
True for CEX-routable Solana tokens, and for EVM native assets plus
Pimlico-listed ERC-20s on Pimlico-supported chains.

hasSelfPrivate.description:
Indicates if token supports private (self-to-self) swaps.
Stored field computed when token is saved.
True when token has CEX support AND at least 2 enabled CEX swap provider mappings.

marketCapChange24h.description: 24h market cap change percentage from CoinGecko.

securityScan.description:
Last security verdict for this token, with the provider's full
response and an `expiresAt` driving re-scan. Absent until the token has
been selected as a swap source or destination at least once.

OrderStatus.description:
- **-2** Order is being initialized (label: INITIALIZING)
- **-1** Order initialized (label: NEW)
- **0** Waiting for deposit confirmation (label: WAITING)
- **1** Deposit is being confirmed (label: CONFIRMING)
- **2** Exchange is in progress (label: EXCHANGING)
- **3** Order is going through anonymization (label: ANONYMIZING)
- **4** Order completed successfully (label: FINISHED)
- **5** Order has expired (label: EXPIRED)
- **6** Order failed (label: FAILED)
- **7** Order was refunded (label: REFUNDED)
- **8** Order was deleted (label: DELETED)

Status.description:
- **0** New swap
- **1** Waiting for confirmation
- **2** Being confirmed
- **3** Exchange in progress
- **4** Sending to destination
- **5** Swap completed
- **6** Swap failed
- **7** Swap refunded
- **8** Verifying swap
- **9** Swap expired
- **10** Fallback mode

Retry a failed multiswap bundle. Only possible while the orders are within 30 minutes
of creation (deposit addresses still valid) — the existing UserOp is reset to PENDING and
`txData` (same shape as POST multi/{multiId}/tx/build) is returned so the frontend can
re-sign and submit immediately.

After 30 minutes, or for REFUNDED orders, this returns 400 — use POST /multi/recovery
to withdraw the stuck funds instead.

get.description:
Returns a public, partner-safe summary of HoudiniSwap API and quote system
availability. This endpoint does not require authentication or x402 payment.

tags.name: Private Swaps
tags.description: Anonymous two-leg swaps routed through a privacy bridge (XMR by default), so the deposit and payout legs are not linkable on-chain. Call `GET /tokens?hasCex=true` for token ids, quote with `types=private`, create with `POST /exchanges`, then track with `GET /orders`. Private-only controls: `anonymous`, `useXmr`, `rotatePayoutWallets`, and the `inLeg*` / `outLeg*` provider filters.

tags.name: Standard Swaps
tags.description: Direct single-leg centralized-exchange swaps — the fastest route, with no privacy hop. Call `GET /tokens?hasCex=true` for token ids, quote with `types=standard`, create with `POST /exchanges`, then track with `GET /orders`. Partner `markup` is supported here.

tags.name: DEX Swaps
tags.description: On-chain swaps signed and funded from the user's own wallet. Call `GET /tokens?hasDex=true` for token ids, quote with `types=dex` (`slippage` applies to DEX only), check and grant token allowance, sign the returned chain signatures, create the exchange, then confirm the broadcast transaction. Partner `markup` is not supported for DEX routes.

tags.name: Multi-Exchange
tags.description: Create and track a group of swaps sharing one `multiId`. Quotes are resolved server-side, so no `quoteId` is required. Each order gets its own deposit address; poll `GET /exchanges/multi/{multiId}` for the status of every leg. Uses CEX standard and private routes — DEX is not supported in a batch. To fund the whole group with one on-chain transaction instead, see Bundler.

tags.name: Bundler
tags.description: Fund an entire multi-exchange group with a single on-chain transaction: Solana batch transfer (up to 10 deposits per batch) or EVM ERC-4337 UserOperation (up to 20 legs per batch). All orders must share the same source token chain — use `GET /tokens?hasBundler=true` to find batchable tokens before creating the group. Build the transaction, submit the signed EVM UserOperation, and if a bundle fails, retry it within 30 minutes or recover stuck assets from the smart account.

tags.name: Reference Data
tags.description: Optional lookups: supported chains, liquidity providers, and per-pair min/max swap amounts. Responses are cached and change rarely — safe to fetch once and reuse. Token ids come from `/tokens`, listed in each swap section above.

tags.name: Partner Account
tags.description: Your partner profile, earned commissions, withdrawals, volume analytics, and the rate-limit budget attached to your API key. Every endpoint is scoped to the partner that owns the key making the request.

tags.name: System
tags.description: Service health. `GET /status` is unauthenticated and exempt from x402 payment — use it for uptime monitoring.
